_comment: Mock provider configuration. This file defines the instrument that every
measurement in this project is taken with, so its parameters are part of the
method and are committed alongside the results.
The price list here is the mock provider's OWN, deliberately separate from the
gateway's pricing table in gateway.example.json. The cost reconciliation
compares two independently computed numbers; if both sides read the same price
list through the same code, a bug in that code cancels out and the
reconciliation passes while both invoices are wrong. The two files are expected
to agree, and the reconciliation is what proves they do.
Latencies are chosen to be realistic but fast enough that a 2000-request
benchmark finishes in seconds: a real provider's TTFB is 200-800ms, and using
that here would make every benchmark a 20-minute affair without changing what
is being measured (the gateway's own overhead is independent of how long the
provider takes).

mock-smart._comment: The expensive tier a degraded-budget route falls back FROM, and the target of the cost-control demonstration.

_comment: A reasoning model. It reports reasoning_tokens inside
completion_tokens_details, which is the trap the pricing package has a
test for: those tokens are ALREADY included in completion_tokens, and
adding them again double-bills a thinking model by roughly 10x.

mock-cached._comment: Reports cached_tokens, exercising the other half-billing trap: prompt_tokens already includes cached_tokens.

_comment: All faults default to off. They are switched on at runtime through the admin
endpoint (POST /admin/fault?down=true), which is how the failover benchmark
kills a provider mid-flight under load rather than restarting it between runs.
Restarting between runs would measure startup, not failover.
